{{nihongo|'''Ime Shrine & Hachimangu'''|伊米神社八幡宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Ime Shrine & Hachimangu''' (いめじんじゃはちまんぐう) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Sakuramachi, {{ill|Ojiya, Niigata|Q819174|qid=Q819174}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is one of the candidate shrines for "Ime Shrine," recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as one of the five seats in {{ill|Uonuma district|Q11674002|qid=Q11674002}}.

=== History ===
Ame-no-Kagoyama-no-Mikoto was ordered to pacify {{ill|Koshi Province (Japan)|de|Provinz Koshi (Japan)|es|Provincia de Koshi (Japón)|ff|Koshi Province (Japan)|fr|Province de Koshi (Japon)|ja|越国|ko|고시국|nl|Koshi (provincie)|pt|Província de Koshi|simple|Koshi Province (Japan)|zh|越國 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Kosi-kok|zh_yue|越國 (日本)|qid=Q1351611}} and arrived in this area. He first lived in Kami-Ime (Ryōshinden, now in Ojiya), later in Shimo-Ime (Sakuramachi), and then in the area called Imegahara, where present-day Ime Hachimangu stands. ''Ime Hachimangu Koshōsho-jō'' records: "Ime-Ōkami is Imehiko-no-Mikoto and settled here; therefore this place is called Imehara. He had one son and one daughter. The elder was named Kamiine Nagaho, and the younger princess was called Imetara-hime... The place where Ime Nagaho-ō sat is now called Kami-Ime, and the place where Imetara-hime sat is called Shimo-Ime." It is also said that while he lived here he was called Tegurihiko-no-Mikoto.

When Minamoto no Yoshiie passed through this area, he fought the local Emishi. His retainer Nagano hid Yoshiie beneath Tōguni Bridge and saved his life. Yoshiie enshrined the protective principal image from inside his helmet as Hachimangu and allowed the Nagano family to govern the area. Another account says that in {{ill|1064|ab|1064|af|1064|als|1064|am|1064 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1064|ar|1064|ary|1064|arz|1064|ast|1064|avk|1064|az|1064|azb|۱۰۶۴ (میلادی)|bcl|1064|be|1064|be_x_old|1064|bg|1064|bn|১০৬৪|bpy|মারি ১০৬৪|br|1064|bs|1064.|ca|1064|cdo|1064 nièng|ceb|1064|ckb|١٠٦٤|crh|1064|cs|1064|cv|1064|cy|1064|da|1064|de|1064|diq|1064|el|1064|eml|1064|eo|1064|es|1064|et|1064|eu|1064|fa|۱۰۶۴ (میلادی)|fi|1064|fo|1064|fr|1064|fy|1064|ga|1064|gan|1064年|gcr|1064|gd|1064|gl|1064|hak|1064-ngièn|he|1064|hi|१०६४|ht|1064 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1064|hy|1064|id|1064|ilo|1064|io|1064|is|1064|it|1064|ja|1064年|jv|1064|ka|1064|kaa|1064|kk|1064 жыл|ko|1064년|la|1064|lb|1064|lij|1064|lmo|1064|lt|1064 m.|lv|1064. gads|map_bms|1064|mdf|1064|mg|1064|mhr|1064|mi|1064|mk|1064|mr|इ.स. १०६४|mrj|1064 и|ms|1064|mzn|۱۰۶۴|nah|1064|nap|1064|nds|1064|new|सन् १०६४|nl|1064|nn|1064|no|1064|nrm|1064|nso|1064|oc|1064|or|୧୦୬୪|os|1064-æм аз|pl|1064|pnb|1064|pt|1064|qu|1064|ro|1064|ru|1064 год|rue|1064|sa|१०६४|scn|1064|sd|1064ع|se|1064|sh|1064.|shn|1064|si|1064|simple|1064|sk|1064|sl|1064|smn|1064|sq|1064|sr|1064|su|1064|sv|1064|sw|1064|tg|Соли 1064|th|พ.ศ. 1607|tk|1064|tl|1064|tly|1064|tr|1064|tt|1064 ел|uk|1064|ur|1064ء|uz|1064|vec|1064|vi|1064|war|1064|wuu|1064年|xmf|1064|zh|1064年|zh_min_nan|1064 nî|zh_yue|1064年|qid=Q19404}}, when Yoshiie returned from Ōshū to Kyoto, he gave thanks for victory and left two retainers (Nagano and Abe, or Nakamachi and Nagano) to guard Hachiman Shrine. After that, Hachimangu was enshrined together with Ime Shrine.

=== Kami-Ime Springs ===
There are two springs: Kami-Ime Spring and Shimo-Ime Spring.
* It is said that drinking while praying to the deity of Ime drives away evil influences and disasters.
* It is said that Kami-Ime Spring helps the left eye, and Shimo-Ime Spring helps the right eye.
* It is said that men are healed by drinking Kami-Ime Spring, and women by drinking Shimo-Ime Spring.

* A legend says that when the wife of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ca|Fujiwara no Tokihira|fa|فوجیوارا نو توکیهیرا|fr|Fujiwara no Tokihira|hr|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ja|藤原時平|pl|Fujiwara no Tokihira|pt|Fujiwara no Tokihira|ru|Фудзивара-но Токихира|sh|Fujiwara no Tokihira|uk|Фудзівара но Токіхіра|zh|藤原時平|qid=Q2994735}} and {{ill|Fujiwara no Kanehira|ja|藤原兼平|qid=Q106234851}} were headed to Yoshidani in Ojiya and had no water, Kanehira faced toward Kyoto and prayed to {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}: "Please forgive the sins of the Fujiwara clan and grant us water." Water then welled up. This came to be called "Water of Deep Emotion," though it is also said the story arose because "Kami-Ime" and "kanmei" sound similar.
